questions.questionTextEn: Find the missing term in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ___, 56.
The price of a laptop is first increased by 20% and then decreased by 25%. What is the net percentage change in its price?
questions.explanationEn: Starting from 100, a 20% increase gives 120. A subsequent 25% decrease reduces it by 0.25 * 120 = 30 to 90. Net change = -10%, i.e., a 10% decrease.

questions.questionTextEn: In a certain code, 'STACK' is coded as 'TUBDL'. How is 'QUEUE' coded in the same language?
questions.explanationEn: Each letter is shifted forward by +1 in the alphabet: S->T, T->U, A->B, C->D, K->L. Applying +1 to QUEUE gives Q->R, U->V, E->F, U->V, E->F => 'RVFVF'.

questions.questionTextEn: Statements: (1) All compilers are translators. (2) Some translators are interpreters. Which conclusion follows with certainty?
questions.explanationEn: From 'All compilers are translators' (assuming compilers exist), its valid conversion is 'Some translators are compilers'. No definite relation between compilers and interpreters is established.

questions.questionTextEn: 15 workers can build a wall in 12 days. Working at the same rate, how many workers are required to build the same wall in 9 days?
questions.explanationEn: Total worker-days = 15 * 12 = 180. For 9 days, workers needed = 180 / 9 = 20.

questions.questionTextEn: Box I contains 3 red and 2 blue balls; Box II contains 2 red and 4 blue balls. A box is chosen at random (equally likely) and one ball is drawn. If the drawn ball is red, what is the probability that it came from Box I?

Passage: 'Open-source software thrives not merely because its code is free to inspect, but because distributed peer review surfaces edge-case defects faster than closed teams can anticipate them. However, critical infrastructure libraries often suffer from maintainer burnout when commercial adopters consume code without contributing back.' Which of the following is the MOST valid inference from the passage?
optionsEn: Closed-source software never has edge-case defects.
Commercial adoption alone guarantees the long-term sustainability of open-source libraries.
Unreciprocated commercial use can strain the sustainability of critical open-source projects.
Peer review eliminates maintainer burnout in open-source ecosystems.
questions.explanationEn: The passage explicitly states that critical libraries suffer maintainer burnout when commercial adopters consume without contributing back, directly supporting option (C).

questions.questionTextEn: A boat takes 3 hours to travel 36 km downstream and 6 hours to return the same 36 km upstream. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.explanationEn: Downstream speed = 36/3 = 12 km/h. Upstream speed = 36/6 = 6 km/h. Speed of stream = (12 - 6)/2 = 3 km/h.

questions.questionTextEn: A diagnostic test for a rare disease (affecting 1% of the population) has 99% sensitivity (true positive rate) and 95% specificity (true negative rate). If a randomly selected person tests positive, what is the approximate probability that they actually have the disease?
questions.explanationEn: Out of 10,000 people: 100 have the disease (99 test positive); 9,900 do not (5% = 495 false positives). P(Disease | +) = 99 / (99 + 495) = 99 / 594 = 1/6 ≈ 16.7%.

questions.questionTextEn: Six friends P, Q, R, S, T, and U sit around a circular table facing the center. P is opposite S. Q is to the immediate left of P. R is between S and T. U is not adjacent to T. Who sits to the immediate right of S?
questions.explanationEn: Number seats 1 to 6 clockwise facing the center. Place P at 1, so S (opposite P) is at 4, and Q (immediate left of P facing center) is at 2. Since R is between S(4) and T, and seat 2 is occupied by Q, we must place R at 5 and T at 6, leaving U at 3 (not adjacent to T). Facing the center from S(4), the immediate right seat is position 3, which is U.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following degree sequences CANNOT represent a simple undirected graph?
questions.explanationEn: In (3, 3, 3, 1) on 4 vertices, three vertices have degree 3, meaning each is adjacent to ALL other 3 vertices. That forces the 4th vertex to have degree 3, contradicting its listed degree of 1.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following propositional logic formulas is a tautology?
questions.explanationEn: By Modus Ponens, if p is true and p -> q is true, then q must be true. Hence (p ∧ (p -> q)) -> q evaluates to True under every truth assignment.

questions.questionTextEn: If P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4, and P(A | B) = 0.5, what is P(B | A)?
questions.explanationEn: P(A ∩ B) = P(A|B)*P(B) = 0.5 * 0.4 = 0.2. Thus P(B|A) = P(A ∩ B)/P(A) = 0.2 / 0.5 = 0.4 (note A and B are independent).

questions.questionTextEn: A full 3-ary tree (every internal node has exactly 3 children) has 10 internal nodes. How many leaf nodes does it have?
questions.explanationEn: In a full k-ary tree with i internal nodes, the number of leaves is L = (k - 1)*i + 1 = (3 - 1)*10 + 1 = 21.

questions.questionTextEn: How many self-dual Boolean functions exist for n = 3 Boolean variables?
questions.explanationEn: A Boolean function on n variables is self-dual if for each of the 2^(n-1) complementary input pairs, f(x') = (f(x))'. Thus there are 2^(2^(n-1)) = 2^(2^2) = 2^4 = 16 self-dual functions for n = 3.

questions.questionTextEn: An unpipelined processor has a cycle time of 20 ns. It is converted into a 5-stage pipeline with stage delays of 3 ns, 5 ns, 4 ns, 6 ns, and 2 ns, plus an inter-stage latch overhead of 1 ns per stage. What is the clock period (in ns) of the pipelined processor?
questions.explanationEn: Pipeline clock period = max(stage delays) + latch overhead = max(3, 5, 4, 6, 2) + 1 = 6 + 1 = 7 ns.

questions.questionTextEn: A machine has 12-bit instructions and 4-bit register addresses. If it supports 14 two-register instructions, what is the maximum number of one-register instructions it can support (assuming no zero-register instructions)?
questions.explanationEn: Two-register instructions use 8 operand bits, leaving 12 - 8 = 4 opcode bits (2^4 = 16 prefixes). Using 14 leaves 2 free prefixes, each expanded by 4 freed register bits: 2 × 2^4 = 32 one-register instructions.

questions.questionTextEn: How many clock cycles are required to complete 100 independent instructions in a 6-stage pipeline with no hazards or stalls?
questions.explanationEn: In an ideal k-stage pipeline, n instructions take k + n - 1 cycles = 6 + 100 - 1 = 105 cycles.

questions.questionTextEn: For a sparse undirected graph with `V` vertices and `E` edges (where `E = O(V)`), what is the space complexity of an adjacency list representation compared to an adjacency matrix?
optionsEn: Adjacency list: O(V^2); Adjacency matrix: O(V + E)
Adjacency list: O(V + E); Adjacency matrix: O(V^2)
questions.explanationEn: An adjacency list stores V list headers and 2E edge entries -> O(V + E). An adjacency matrix always allocates a V × V grid -> O(V^2).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following properties hold for every complete binary tree with `n` nodes (height of a single-node tree = 0)?
optionsEn: All levels except possibly the last are completely filled
Nodes on the last level are filled from left to right
The height of the tree is floor(log2(n))
Every internal node has exactly two children
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and C are defining properties of a complete binary tree. An internal node on the second-to-last level may have only a left child if n is even, so D is false.

questions.questionTextEn: For any positive integer `n`, the C expression `(n & (n - 1)) == 0` evaluates to true (1) if and only if:
optionsEn: n has an even number of 1-bits
questions.explanationEn: Subtracting 1 flips the rightmost 1-bit to 0 and all trailing 0s to 1. Thus `n & (n - 1)` clears the lowest set bit; for n > 0, the result is 0 iff n has exactly one 1-bit (a power of 2).

questions.questionTextEn: In Bellman-Ford's algorithm on a graph with 9 vertices and 20 edges, how many edge-relaxation iterations (passes over all edges) are performed in the main loop before the negative-cycle check?
questions.explanationEn: Any simple shortest path in a graph of V vertices has at most V - 1 edges, so Bellman-Ford runs `V - 1 = 9 - 1 = 8` passes.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider 5 activities with (start, finish) times: A(1, 4), B(3, 5), C(0, 6), D(5, 7), E(8, 9). What is the maximum number of mutually non-overlapping activities that can be scheduled?
questions.explanationEn: Sorted by finish time: A(1,4), B(3,5), C(0,6), D(5,7), E(8,9). Greedy selects A(1,4), skips B and C (overlap), selects D(5,7), selects E(8,9). Maximum = 3.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following language classes are CLOSED under complementation?
questions.explanationEn: Regular, DCFL, and Recursive languages are all closed under complementation. RE languages are NOT closed under complementation (e.g., `HALT` is RE, while `HALT'` is not RE).

questions.questionTextEn: Over the alphabet `Σ = {a, b, c}`, how many strings have length at most 3 (including the empty string `ε`)?
A Context-Free Grammar G is said to be ambiguous if:
optionsEn: There exists at least one string in L(G) with two or more distinct parse trees (or leftmost derivations)
questions.explanationEn: Ambiguity means at least one string in `L(G)` has two or more distinct derivation trees (equivalently, two distinct leftmost derivations).

questions.questionTextEn: How many tokens are in the C expression `a+++b` according to the maximal munch rule?
questions.explanationEn: Maximal munch groups `a` (identifier), `++` (post-increment), `+` (binary addition), and `b` (identifier) — 4 tokens.

questions.questionTextEn: For the same three processes arriving at time 0 with burst times 10, 4, and 6 ms, what is the average waiting time (in ms) under non-preemptive SJF scheduling?
questions.explanationEn: Execution order: P2 (4), P3 (6), P1 (10). Waiting times: P2 = 0, P3 = 4, P1 = 10. Average = `(0 + 4 + 10) / 3 = 14 / 3 = 4.67 ms`.

questions.questionTextEn: A running process executes a blocking `read()` system call on a disk file. To which state does the OS transition this process?
questions.explanationEn: A blocking I/O request suspends the process in the Waiting (Blocked) queue until the disk I/O completes, after which an interrupt moves it back to the Ready queue.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following three requirements must ANY correct solution to the Critical Section Problem satisfy?
questions.explanationEn: The three formal correctness criteria are Mutual Exclusion, Progress, and Bounded Waiting. Busy waiting (spinlocks, Peterson's) is permitted in valid solutions (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: Which integrity constraint ensures that a foreign key value in a referencing table must either match an existing primary key value in the referenced table or be `NULL`?
questions.explanationEn: Referential integrity enforces consistency across foreign-key references so no dangling references point to non-existent tuples.

questions.questionTextEn: Given `R(A, B, C, D, E, F)` and FDs `{A -> BC, CD -> E, B -> D, E -> A}`, how many attributes are in the closure `{A}^+`?
questions.explanationEn: `A -> BC` gives `{A,B,C}`; `B -> D` adds `D` (`{A,B,C,D}`); `CD -> E` adds `E` (`{A,B,C,D,E}`). `F` is never derived. Total = 5 attributes.

questions.questionTextEn: In a Stop-and-Wait protocol, the frame transmission time is `T_t = 2 ms` and the one-way propagation delay is `T_p = 4 ms` (ACK transmission time is negligible). What is the link utilization (efficiency) percentage?
A signal travels over a 3000 km fiber-optic link at a propagation speed of `2 × 10^8` m/s. What is the one-way propagation delay in milliseconds?

A token bucket shaper has a bucket capacity of 2 MB and a token arrival rate of 1 MB/s. The maximum output link rate is 5 MB/s. Starting with a full bucket, what is the maximum burst duration (in seconds) at peak rate 5 MB/s?
questions.explanationEn: Burst duration `S = C / (M - r) = 2 MB / (5 - 1 MB/s) = 2 / 4 = 0.5` seconds.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the coefficient of x^10 in the power series expansion of (1 - x)^(-4)?
The system of equations x + y + z = 6, 2x + 3y + 4z = 20, x + 2y + 3z = 14 has infinitely many solutions. What is the dimension of the null space of the coefficient matrix?
questions.explanationEn: Row 2 equals Row 1 + Row 3 ([1, 1, 1] + [1, 2, 3] = [2, 3, 4]), while Row 1 and Row 3 are linearly independent. Hence the coefficient matrix has rank 2, so nullity = 3 - 2 = 1.

questions.questionTextEn: How many ways can 10 identical candies be distributed among 3 children such that the first child gets at least 2 candies, the second gets at least 1 candy, and the third gets at least 0 candies?
questions.explanationEn: Give 2 to child 1 and 1 to child 2 first, leaving 10 - 3 = 7 identical candies for 3 children with no lower bounds. By stars and bars: C(7 + 3 - 1, 3 - 1) = C(9, 2) = 36.

questions.questionTextEn: Let A be a 4×4 skew-symmetric real matrix (A^T = -A). Which of the following is ALWAYS true about the eigenvalues of A?
optionsEn: All eigenvalues are purely imaginary or zero.
The determinant of A is always 0.
questions.explanationEn: For a real skew-symmetric matrix, every eigenvalue λ satisfies λ = -conj(λ), so Re(λ) = 0 (purely imaginary or 0). Note det(A) need not be 0 for even n = 4 (e.g. block diagonal rotation matrices).

questions.questionTextEn: What is the minimum number of states required in a Moore machine to detect the overlapping binary sequence '1011' on a serial input stream?
questions.explanationEn: A Moore machine detecting a pattern of length k requires at least k + 1 states: S0 (no match), S1 ('1'), S2 ('10'), S3 ('101'), and S4 ('1011', output=1). Thus 5 states are required.

questions.questionTextEn: What decimal value is represented by the 32-bit IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point number 0xC1A80000?
Consider doubling the block size of a cache while keeping total cache capacity and associativity unchanged. Which of the following statements are TRUE?
optionsEn: The number of sets in the cache is halved
The number of tag bits per cache line increases by 1
The number of block offset bits increases by 1
The total size of the tag directory decreases
questions.explanationEn: Doubling block size adds 1 offset bit (C), halves the number of lines and sets (A), which decreases index bits by 1 so tag bits per line stay UNCHANGED (B is false). With half as many lines and the same tag width, total tag directory size halves (D is true).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about DMA and I/O architectures are TRUE?
optionsEn: Memory-mapped I/O uses standard load/store instructions to communicate with device registers
Isolated (port-mapped) I/O requires dedicated IN and OUT instructions
In burst-mode DMA, the DMA controller holds the bus until an entire block is transferred
DMA completely eliminates the need for interrupts in a computer system
questions.explanationEn: Memory-mapped I/O shares the memory address space (A), isolated I/O uses separate I/O instructions (B), and burst DMA holds the bus for the whole block (C). DMA still uses an interrupt to signal transfer completion (D is false).

questions.questionTextEn: An L1 cache is 32 KB and an L2 cache is 256 KB. What is the maximum amount of unique data (in KB) that can be held simultaneously in the L1 + L2 cache hierarchy if the hierarchy is strictly exclusive?
questions.explanationEn: In a strictly exclusive cache hierarchy, no block resides in both L1 and L2 simultaneously, so the effective combined capacity is 32 KB + 256 KB = 288 KB (whereas an inclusive hierarchy holds at most 256 KB).

questions.questionTextEn: In Floyd's cycle-finding algorithm (tortoise moving 1 step and hare moving 2 steps per iteration) on a singly linked list with a cycle of length `L` and a non-cyclic tail of length `μ >= 1`, once both pointers meet inside the cycle, resetting one pointer to `head` and advancing both by 1 step at a time causes them to meet at:
optionsEn: A node at distance L/2 from the cycle start
The exact starting node of the cycle
The last node of the cycle
They are not guaranteed to meet again
questions.explanationEn: If they meet at distance `k` into the cycle, `2(μ + k) - (μ + k) = μ + k = c·L` for some integer `c >= 1`, so `μ = c·L - k`. Advancing both pointers by `μ` steps moves the head pointer to the cycle start and the other pointer by `c·L - k` steps back to the exact same cycle start.

`fun(3)`: `d` becomes `1+3=4`, calls `fun(2)` + `d`. `fun(2)`: `d` becomes `4+2=6`, calls `fun(1)` + `d`. `fun(1)` returns current `d = 6`. Unwinding: `fun(2)` returns `6 + 6 = 12`; `fun(3)` returns `12 + 6 = 18` (because `d` is static and equals 6 when `fun(2)` returns).
For any two non-negative integers `a` and `b`, `(a & b) + (a | b) == a + b` because `a & b` captures carry bits and `a | b` captures union bits. Hence `45 + 27 = 72`.
Call 1: n=1, k=1 -> n=2, k=2, calls f(2). Call 2: n=2, k=2 -> n=4, k=3, calls f(4). Call 3: n=4, k=3 -> n=7, k=4, calls f(7). Call 4: n=7 >= 5 -> returns 7.

questions.questionTextEn: Three matrices have dimensions A(5×10), B(10×20), C(20×4). What is the minimum number of scalar multiplications to compute A·B·C?
Consider `T(n) = 16T(n/4) + n^2 log n`. If `T(n) = Θ(n^a (log n)^b)`, what is the value of `a + b`?
questions.explanationEn: Here `n^(log_4 16) = n^2`, and `f(n) = n^2 (log n)^1`. By the extended Master Theorem (Case 2 with `k = 1`), `T(n) = Θ(n^2 (log n)^2)`, so `a = 2, b = 2`, giving `a + b = 4`.

questions.questionTextEn: A 0/1 knapsack has capacity W = 7. Four items have (weight, value): (1, 1), (3, 4), (4, 5), (5, 7). What is the maximum total value that can be packed?
questions.explanationEn: Taking items (3, 4) and (4, 5) uses weight 3 + 4 = 7 and yields value 4 + 5 = 9. Taking (5, 7) leaves capacity 2, which only fits (1, 1) for total value 8. Thus maximum is 9.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following languages over `Σ = {a, b}` are NOT regular?
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and D require unbounded counting or copying and fail the Regular Pumping Lemma. C is a finite language (at most 101 strings), and every finite language is regular.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the minimum number of states in a DFA over `Σ = {a, b}` that accepts all strings containing the substring `"aab"`?
questions.explanationEn: States track progress toward `"aab"`: `q0` (none), `q1` (`a`), `q2` (`aa`), and `q3` (`aab`, accepting sink state). All 4 are distinguishable, so minimum = 4 states.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the grammar:
`S -> L = R | R`
`L -> * R | id`
`R -> L`
Why is this grammar NOT SLR(1)?
optionsEn: In the state containing `S -> L . = R` and `R -> L .`, `=` belongs to `FOLLOW(R)`, causing a Shift-Reduce conflict on `=`
It has a Reduce-Reduce conflict on `id`
questions.explanationEn: Because `S -> L = R` and `L -> * R` and `R -> L`, `FOLLOW(R)` contains `=` (since `S -> L = R -> * R = R`). In the state with `S -> L . = R` and `R -> L .`, SLR(1) shifts on `=` and also reduces `R -> L` on `=`, creating a Shift-Reduce conflict (though the grammar IS LALR(1) and CLR(1)).

questions.topicTag: Compiler Design — Three-Address Code Minimum Registers
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the basic block:
`t1 = a + b`
`t2 = c + d`
`t3 = t1 - t2`
`t4 = t3 * e`
Assuming `a, b, c, d, e` are in memory and `t1..t4` are dead after the block (except `t4`), what is the minimum number of CPU registers needed if instructions can take one register and one memory operand (e.g., `ADD R1, b`)?
questions.explanationEn: `R1 = a; R1 += b;` (`t1` in R1). `R2 = c; R2 += d;` (`t2` in R2). `R1 -= R2;` (`t3` in R1). `R1 *= e;` (`t4` in R1). Only 2 registers are needed.

questions.questionTextEn: Tail Call Optimization (TCO) allows a compiler to compile a tail-recursive function so that it executes using:
optionsEn: O(1) stack space by reusing the current activation record (turning the call into a jump)
O(n) heap space instead of stack space
questions.explanationEn: When the recursive call is the very last action before returning, the current stack frame is no longer needed and can be overwritten in place, turning recursion into an O(1)-space loop.

questions.topicTag: OS — Demand Paging Effective Access Time
questions.questionTextEn: A demand-paged memory system has a main memory access time of 100 ns. Servicing a page fault takes 10 ms (10,000,000 ns) on average. To ensure the Effective Access Time (EAT) does not exceed 200 ns, what is the maximum tolerable page-fault rate `p`?

A disk has cylinders 0 to 199. The head is at cylinder 40 moving UPWARD toward 199. Pending requests are `{10, 25, 70, 120}`. Under the LOOK algorithm (reverses at the highest request without going to 199), what is the total head movement?
questions.explanationEn: Head moves up `40 -> 70 -> 120` (distance `80`), then reverses `120 -> 25 -> 10` (distance `110`). Total = `80 + 110 = 190` cylinders.

questions.questionTextEn: A 16 GB disk partition uses 4 KB blocks. Free blocks are tracked using a bitmap (1 bit per block). What is the size of the bitmap in KB (1 KB = 1024 bytes)?
questions.explanationEn: Total blocks = `16 GB / 4 KB = 2^34 / 2^12 = 2^22` blocks = `2^22` bits = `2^19` bytes = `512 KB`.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider `R(A, B, C, D)` with FDs `{AB -> C, B -> D}`. Why does `R` violate Second Normal Form (2NF)?
optionsEn: Because non-prime attribute `D` is partially dependent on proper subset `B` of candidate key `AB`
questions.explanationEn: The sole candidate key is `AB`, so `C` and `D` are non-prime. Since `B -> D` has a proper subset of a candidate key on the LHS and a non-prime attribute on the RHS, it is a partial dependency violating 2NF.

questions.questionTextEn: A sorted data file has 4096 disk blocks. A sparse primary index fits 16 entries per index block, and multi-level indexing is built on top of it until a single root index block remains. How many total disk block accesses (including the final data block read) are needed to search for a record by its primary key?
questions.explanationEn: Level 1 index: `4096 / 16 = 256` blocks. Level 2 index: `256 / 16 = 16` blocks. Level 3 (root): `16 / 16 = 1` block. Search reads 3 index levels + 1 data block = 4 disk block accesses.

questions.questionTextEn: What does the Tuple Relational Calculus query `{ t.name | Employee(t) ∧ ¬(∃s)(Employee(s) ∧ s.salary > t.salary) }` return?
optionsEn: Names of all employees except the highest paid
Names of employees earning the minimum salary
Names of employees with duplicate salaries
Names of employees earning the maximum salary
questions.explanationEn: `¬(∃s)(s.salary > t.salary)` means no employee earns strictly more than `t`, selecting all employees who earn the maximum salary.

questions.questionTextEn: A network has 12 routers and 20 bidirectional links. If one router originates a Link-State Advertisement (LSA) and floods it (each router forwards a newly seen LSA on all links except the one it arrived on), how many total LSA copies are guaranteed to traverse the network AT LEAST once per link? Specifically, in a tree topology of 12 routers (11 links), how many total link transmissions occur to flood one LSA from a single root router to all other routers?
questions.explanationEn: In a tree of 12 routers (11 links), each non-root router receives the LSA exactly once over its parent link and forwards only to its children, so each of the 11 links carries the LSA exactly once: 11 transmissions.

questions.questionTextEn: Host A has IP address `172.16.45.130/25`. Which of the following IP addresses is on the EXACT SAME subnet as Host A?
questions.explanationEn: A `/25` mask splits the last octet into `0..127` and `128..255`. Since `130 ∈ [128, 255]`, Host A's subnet is `172.16.45.128/25` (usable hosts `.129` to `.254`), which includes `172.16.45.200`.

questions.questionTextEn: A single 2000-byte packet travels from Host A to Host B across 2 routers (3 links). Each link has bandwidth 10 Mbps (`10^7` bps) and propagation delay 5 ms. What is the total end-to-end delay in milliseconds (ignoring queueing and processing delays)?
